scope-binary-data-load-stage: Section 1, p.5: the paper states in its own overview that it covers binary data loading from the classical to the quantum domain and formatting into states.
scope-gate-model-circuits: Section 2.1, p.6: the paper states it is concerned with the gate based model and presents circuits in a gate based framework.
state-format-matrix-three-qubits: Section 2.1, p.6, Equation 1: the paper defines the three-qubit state psi_A (row qubit, column qubit, value qubit) for the 2 by 2 bit matrix.
normalization-dropped: Section 2.1, p.6: the paper states its notation convention of dropping the overall normalization constant.
family1-requirements-table1: Section 2.2, Figure 5 and Table 1, p.7-9: N qubits, N gates and depth 1 follow by construction from the one-gate-per-bit circuit the paper defines; text states each count.
family1-parallel-gates: Section 2.2, p.8: the paper defines the cost measure (N gates in parallel, gate depth as execution time) for the circuit it defines.
cswap-multi-qubit-needed: Section 2.4.4, p.15: the paper states the design need (swap of more than two bits) and that multi-pair controlled swaps are used in the circuits that follow. A statement of what the paper builds.
compression-on-classical-computer: Section 2.5.1, p.21: 'In our scheme the compression algorithm is implemented on a classical computer.' The paper's own scheme design.
family2-hadamard-count: Section 3.3.1, Equation 15, p.28-29: N/2 + N/4 + ... summed in full with the geometric identity (Equation 14) for N = 2^n; gives N - 1. It matches the three Hadamard gates in Figure 7 for N = 4. A derivation, not a labelled theorem.
family2-cswap-count: Section 3.3.2, Equations 16-18, p.29-30: the weighted sum of k N/2^k is derived in full for N = 2^n and gives 2N - n - 2. The N = 4 check against Figures 7 and 25 (four CSwap gates) holds.
circuits-verified-by-simulation-only: Section 5, p.37: the authors state all circuit families, in both forms, were simulated in Quipper. The value says only that, and claims no simulation result. The id word 'only' is not in the value.
family1-one-qubit-per-bit-depth-1: Section 2.2, p.7-8: the paper defines family #1 as one qubit and one gate per bit and states depth 1 for the family, by construction.
family1-state-not-optimal-for-speedup: Section 2.2, p.9: the paper itself states that its family #1 state (Equation 2) is not optimal for exponential-speedup algorithms and uses this to motivate family #2. A caveat on its own circuit.
future-work-distribution-shift: Section 5, p.6: the paper names distribution shift, model-specific uncertainty and pretraining distributions as open work.
conformal-setup-lac-090: Section 3.1, p.3: the paper states the LAC score and target coverage 0.90 it uses.
conformal-calibration-quantile: Section 3.1, p.3: the paper defines the calibration quantile and the prediction set, with a calibration set disjoint from training.
sscs-definition-min-over-sizes: Section 3.2, p.3: the paper defines SSC(k) over groups G_k and SSCS as the minimum over k.
coverage-rate-and-set-size-definitions: Section 3.2, p.3: the paper defines CR as the proportion of test samples whose label lies in the set, and SS as the mean set size.
conditional-coverage-two-group-example: Section 3.2, p.4: a hypothetical two-group illustration, with invented numbers (60 percent, 100 percent, 90 percent), of the conditional-coverage idea behind the defined metric. It is stated as an example, not as a measurement.
benchmark-setup-models-datasets: Section 3.3, p.4: the four model families and the 112 datasets (up to 10 classes, up to 10000 samples) as the paper states them.
benchmark-setup-split-and-auc: Section 3.3, p.4: 80/20 train and calibration split, validation tuning, test reporting and weighted one-vs-one AUC, as stated.
results-averaged-15-seeds: Section 4, p.4: 'Results are averaged over 15 seeds.' Table 1 caption agrees (112 datasets and 15 seeds).
tfm-scope-limit: Section 5, p.6: the paper states its analysis is limited to small and medium datasets and to a model-agnostic conformal framework.
hqsl-architecture: Section 1, p.2: the paper defines HQSL as a classical client-side model plus a server-side quantum layer followed by classical layers.
assumption-clients-classical-only: Section 4.2.2, p.13: the paper states the assumption that clients have classical resources and no quantum resources, referring to Section 3.
circuit6-definition: Section 4.2.1, p.9-11: Circuit 6 is defined as two qubits, a 3-dimensional input encoded at three RX points per qubit, depth 8, 6 parameters and no layer repetition. Appendix C agrees.
qubit-efficient-cost-depth-grows: Section 4.2.1, p.11: the paper states that depth grows with input dimension and that it therefore restricts itself to 3 dimensions on 2 qubits.
classical-counterpart-definition: Section 4.2.1, p.13: the paper defines the classical counterpart as a dense layer with 3 inputs, 2 outputs and ReLU.
hqsl-variants-definition: Section 4.2.2, p.13-14 and Figure 6: the paper defines variant 1 (4 dense layers, 7 inputs, 3-dim smashed data) and variant 2 (two convolutional filters, 2 dense layers down to 3).
quantum-layer-measurement-shots: Sections 4.1 and 4.2.3, p.7 and 16: Pauli-Y observable per qubit and a default of 1000 shots, as stated.
multi-client-round-robin: Section 4.3, p.16: the paper states its K-client method follows the basic round-robin protocol and describes the weight hand-off.
multi-client-comm-overhead-out-of-scope: Section 4.3, p.16, and Section 5.2, p.25: the paper states communication efficiency is out of scope and that round-robin raises per-client latency as clients grow.
software-and-simulation-setup: Section 5, p.18: Python 3.11.3, PyTorch 2.1.0, PennyLane simulation and an RTX 2080 Ti machine, as stated.
datasets-table3-sizes: Section 5, Table 3, p.19: the training and testing sizes match the table (800/200, 455/114, 4800/1200, 4800/1200, 6388/1597).
evaluation-protocol-5fold: Section 5, p.18: fixed seed, five non-overlapping folds, four folds for training and one for testing.
training-hyperparameters: Section 5.1, p.20: Adam, learning rate 1e-3 (1e-4 for Speech Commands), 100 epochs for the two multivariate sets and 50 for the three image sets, as stated.
hardware-eval-setup: Section 5.1, p.21: the paper states it limited the hardware and noisy-simulator evaluation to one fold of Botnet DGA, trained on default.qubit.
multi-client-setup: Section 5.2, p.24: IID split into K subsets for K in {2,3,4,5,10,20,50,100}, 100 or 50 global epochs, one fold only, as stated.
multi-client-limits-iid-roundrobin: Section 5.2, p.24-25: the paper states it used IID data and only round-robin and defers unbalanced data, advanced protocols and latency reduction.
threat-model-setup: Section 6.1.1, p.26: the paper states its honest-but-curious server, disjoint auxiliary dataset, inference-time attacks and that training-time leakage is not addressed.
fidelity-expectation-derivation: Section 6.1.3, Equations 9-12, p.29-30: derived in full for one RX-encoded qubit in |0> with Laplace(0, b) noise. F = cos^2(eta/2) from the state vectors and E[cos eta] = 1/(1 + b^2) from the Laplace characteristic function. Both steps are correct.
noise-defense-experiment-setup: Section 6.2, p.32: mu in {0,pi,2pi,3pi,4pi}, b in {0.01,0.1,0.5,1}, SGD 1e-3 with momentum 0.9, 200 epochs, noise layer added after training.
limit-prototype-small-circuit-future-wor: Section 7, p.42: the paper states the prototype is a small shallow circuit and lists scaling as future work.
limit-other-attacks-open: Section 7, p.42: the paper names model inversion, membership inference and quantum-specific attacks as open.
limit-future-topologies-fl-baselines: Section 7, p.42: the paper names U-shaped splits, vertical partition and FL and QFL baselines as not yet done.
appendix-d-cosine-distance: Appendix D, Equations 13-14, p.45: cosine distance defined as 1 minus cosine similarity, range 0 to 2.
appendix-d-dssim-clipped-ssim: Appendix D, Equation 16, p.46-47: SSIM redefined as max(SSIM, 0) and DSSIM = (1 - SSIM)/2 in [0, 0.5], as stated.
reconstruction-masking-function: Section 6.2, p.33: the masking function and batch means are described as the paper's own evaluation procedure.
cowlessur-privacy-open: Section 7, p.42: the paper says a rigorous theoretical analysis (differential privacy, adaptive adversaries) remains open.
cowlessur-small-circuit: Section 1, p.3 and Section 7, p.42: the paper states it uses a low-depth 2-qubit circuit and that the prototype is small and shallow.
scope-abstract: Abstract, p.1: the paper states what it describes, formalizes, explores and demonstrates.
scope-pegasus-reference-wms: Section 1, p.2: the paper states its focus on scientific applications and Pegasus as the reference WMS architecture.
definition-scientific-workflow-dag: Section 3.1, Definition 3.1, p.2: a workflow is defined as a DAG W = (T, E).
hybrid-pipeline-five-steps: Section 3.4, p.3: the five pipeline steps of Figure 1 are described as the paper's own model.
definition-vqa-hybrid-loop: Section 3.4, p.4: 'VQAs can be defined as' hybrid algorithms with an iteratively optimized parametrized circuit. The paper's stated working definition.
definition-hybrid-workflow-tuple: Section 4.1, Definition 4.1, p.5-6: W = (T, Q, E, D, f) with the components as listed. The definition writes T' subset of T, while the text says subset or equal.
assumption-user-defined-mapping-f: Section 4.1, p.4: the paper states the assumption that the user defines f (the reason cited to [67]) and that f is surjective but not injective by its model.
definition-quantum-candidate: Section 4.1, Equation 1, p.4: quantum candidates and the decision-node insertion are defined by the paper.
definition-three-quantum-task-types: Section 4.1, Figure 3, p.4-5: circuit, task and hybrid execution are defined as the paper states.
definition-compute-intensive-70pct: Section 5.1, p.6-7: the paper defines compute-intensive as at least 70 percent of execution time in floating-point operations.
candidate-criteria-three: Section 5.1, p.6-7: the three selection criteria are listed in the paper as those used. Items (ii) and (iii) are in the passage though the quotes show only (i).
use-case-two-quantum-candidates: Section 5.1, p.7: the paper names the two tasks (distance matrix by SWAP test, LEBM by VQE) as the candidates in its use case.
fig4b-two-decision-nodes: Section 5.2, Figure 4b, p.7: the paper defines its own hybrid workflow for the use case, with decision nodes D0 and D1 and their roles.
vqe-error-function-mse: Section 5.2, Equation 3, p.8: the paper defines Err as the mean square error between classic and VQE largest eigenvalues over a matrix set.
setup-5-qubit-ibmq-16x16: Section 5.2, p.8: the paper states runs used 5-qubit IBMQ hardware with a maximum 16 by 16 block dimension.
decision-node-function: Section 5.3.1, Figure 7, p.10: the paper defines the role of decision nodes (control and data flow, monitoring layer, task repository, performance evaluation).
hybrid-wms-six-components: Section 6.1, p.11-12: the paper defines its six architecture components, each with a stated role.
limit-mapping-currently-manual: Section 6.1, p.11: 'Currently, the mapping of quantum candidates into quantum tasks is performed manually by the application developer.'
execution-flow-classic-vs-quantum-task: Section 6.2, p.12: the paper defines the envisioned execution flow for classic and quantum tasks, with the codebase check and the decision-node choice.
assumption-circuit-model-focus: Section 6.3, p.12: the paper states its repository and transpilation descriptions focus on the quantum circuit model, naming superconducting and ion-trapped machines and noting photonics.
limit-descriptors-ibm-centric: Section 6.3, p.12: the paper states its descriptors follow IBM Qiskit definitions and might not apply to annealers or photonics.
challenge-hardware-descriptors: Section 7.1, p.12: the paper names descriptor identification as its first open challenge, with empirical studies and benchmarks required.
challenge-performance-models: Section 7.2, p.13: the paper names performance models as required by schedulers and hard to generalize across architectures.
challenge-optimization-hybrid-workflows: Section 7.3, p.13: the paper lists optimization areas as challenges to be addressed at execution time.
challenge-integration-wms: Section 7.5, p.14: the paper names integration of quantum machines into the HPC continuum through a WMS as its final open challenge.
future-work-photonic-annealers-mbqc: Section 8, p.14: the paper states its plans for photonic, annealer and measurement-based work and more use cases.
swap-test-single-execution-per-pair: Appendix F, p.25: 'we perform a single execution for each C-alpha atom pair', so n executions for n pairs, as the paper states about its own runs.
encoding-padding-three-qubits-eight-dims: Appendix F, p.25, Figure F.10: the 4-coordinate padding for a 2-qubit register and the 8-entry concatenated pair vector on 3 qubits, as the paper states.
theorem2-bipartite-matrix-hermitian: Appendix E, Theorem 2, p.24: stated and proved from the block form of B_IJ with real E_IJ (B^dagger = B), then 'real symmetric implies Hermitian', a textbook step. Real eigenvalues follow in the paper's text.
cranganore-hybrid-wms-architecture: Section 8, p.14: the paper states that, starting from its MD use case, it describes a possible hybrid WMS architecture and identifies the software components.
cranganore-limit-code-classification-lab: Section 6.3, p.12: the paper states its code-classification approach assumes a label for each classic task and depends on the training corpus.
cranganore-limit-photonic-circuit-model: Section 6.3, p.12: the paper states that circuit synthesis and mapping might not guarantee best performance on photonic machines. The premise (best performance with the measurement-based model) is cited to [94]; the HIGH covers the stated caveat, not that premise.
geko-extension-of-gasp: Section III, p.4: the paper names its framework GEKO as an extension of GASP.
definition-quantum-kernel-fidelity: Section II.B, Equations 17-18, p.3: the kernel is defined as the squared overlap of states encoded by U(X) on |0>.
definition-entropy-of-entanglement: Section II.D, Equation 28, p.4: entropy of entanglement defined as the average of the per-qubit von Neumann entropies, with rho_i the partial trace for qubit i.
method-supervised-unsupervised-fitness: Section III.A, p.5-6: the paper defines the supervised technique (QSVM training accuracy as fitness) and the unsupervised technique (eigenvalue analysis, no labels).
method-selection-validation-binary-searc: Section III.A, p.6 and Algorithm 1: selection by training fitness, validation gate, fixed generations or threshold, and binary search on gene count, as stated.
setup-mutation-probability-5-qubits: Section III.A, p.5: 5 qubits per circuit, k mutated copies, mutation probability 50 percent for these results.
setup-pca-95-variance: Section III.A, p.5: PCA to the number of components explaining 95 percent of the variance, as stated.
setup-datasets-synthetic-real: Section IV.A, p.7: the three synthetic sets (400 points each) and six real sets, with all data points used, as stated.
setup-split-20-48-32-scaling-10-tests: Section IV.A, p.7: 20/48/32 test, train and validation split, scaling to [-pi/2, pi/2] and 10 repeats, as stated.
setup-qnn-two-qubits-feature-map: Section III.B, p.6: 2 qubits per circuit, GA-optimised feature map, then a linear CNOT and Rx Ry Rz variational layer trained classically.
setup-qnn-splits-10-80-10: Section IV.B, p.9: 10/80/10 split, scaling and 10 repeats. The sentence names only 'Moons, XOR, and data sets' (a dropped word), but Section III.B names Moons, XOR and Circles and Section IV.B says three sets.
future-work-larger-datasets-other-optimi: Section V, p.10: the paper names larger datasets, other optimisers and a combined fitness as future work.
data-availability-on-request: Section VIII, p.11: the paper states datasets are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request.
definition-pauli-expansion-baseline-kern: Section II.B, Equations 19-21, p.3-4: the repeated H^n U_phi layers, the Pauli-string sum and the data mapping phi_S are written out as the paper's kernel.
gasp-method-scope: Abstract, p.1: the paper states it applies the GASP framework to gate sequence selection in QSVM kernel circuits.

theory_low.family2-packs-into-log-qubits: Section 2.3, p.9-11: an authors' claim about family #2 with no proof at that point. The paper's own Table 3 and Figure 7 also show more than Log2(N) qubits in use (3 qubits for the N=4 state, 6 or 7 in total).
theory_low.fig7-four-bits-three-qubits: Section 2.3, Figure 7, p.11: the output state of the layout is asserted from a circuit figure. It is not derived in the text. A design description, not a proved result.
theory_low.gate-identity-swap-three-cnot: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 2.4.1, p.12, SWAP from three CNOT gates is shown as a figure only.
theory_low.cswap-output-state: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 2.4.2, p.13, Equation 4 gives the controlled-swap output with no derivation.
theory_low.gate-identity-cswap-toffoli: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 2.4.3, p.13-14, the CSWAP from Toffoli gates is shown in Figures 11 and 12 with no derivation.
theory_low.gate-identity-toffoli-decomposition: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 2.4.3, p.14-15, the Toffoli decomposition is shown in Figure 13 only.
theory_low.discarded-qubits-entangled: Section 2.5, p.15-16: 'typically entangled' is a general claim. The paper shows it only for the Equation 5 example, not as a proved statement.
theory_low.junk-qubit-product-state-reuse: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 2.5, p.17, a product-state qubit can be removed without affecting the rest; correlation versus entanglement is asserted, not derived.
theory_low.disentangling-op-from-qec: Section 2.5, p.18: the inspiration from QEC and the 'innovation' are the authors' interpretation and claim. Gate-level correctness of Figure 17 is not argued here.
theory_low.table2-disentangled-product-states: Section 2.5, Table 2, p.18-19: a worked four-case table of one circuit, not a stated theorem. It rests on the gates in Figure 17, which the text does not list.
theory_low.ancilla-measures-parity: Section 2.5, p.18: the parity reading ('as in QEC') is the authors' interpretation. Table 2 is consistent with it but no statement is proved.
theory_low.measuring-q3-a-gains-no-information: Section 2.5, p.18: an informal argument that measuring q3 and the ancilla leaves the superposition intact. No proof.
theory_low.disentangling-iterative: Section 2.5, p.18-19: an authors' claim ('onion peeling' footnote). No worked proof for the four discarded qubits of Figure 7.
theory_low.iid-equiprobable-no-benefit: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 2.5.1, p.20, an information-theory consequence of Shannon coding, stated without proof.
theory_low.compression-block-length-entropy: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 2.5.1, p.21, L as average entropy and the block map N to L N rest on Shannon source coding, stated not derived.
theory_low.compression-example-p003-n100: Section 2.5.1, p.21-22: M = 0.2 N is read from the curve in Figure 23 (the reading matches the figure) and then applied to N = 100. A figure-based worked example, not a proved result.
theory_low.fig23-entropy-curve: Figure 23, p.23: a value read from a figure is never HIGH on the figure alone. The reading checks out on the rendered page (L is 0 at p = 0, near 1 at p = 0.5, red dot near p = 0.03, L = 0.2).
theory_low.decompression-depth-argument: Section 2.5.2, p.22-24: the 'proof' reduces to the existence of classical O(Log N)-depth decompression circuits, cited as 'many classical decompression algorithms' with no specific result. A sketch, not a proof in this paper.
theory_low.family2-hadamard-cswap-per-layer: Section 3.1.1, p.26: the per-layer gate counts are read off the recursion diagram and stated, not derived.
theory_low.family2-depth-log-squared: Section 3.1.1, Equations 10-12, p.26-27: gate counts are tallied as serial from the figure, and the O(n^2) bound is an informal tally. 'Acceptable, but not ideal' is the authors' judgement. Table 3 (gate depth Log2(N)) does not match Equation 12 in the text layer.
theory_low.family2-qubit-total-eq13: Section 3.2, Equation 13, p.27: the geometric sum is right arithmetic, but the premise fails against the paper's own Figure 7. For N = 4 Figure 7 uses 4 data qubits plus 3 Hadamard qubits = 7 qubits (2N - 1), while Equation 13 gives 2N - 2 = 6. The Hadamard count N - 1 in Equation 15 agrees with Figure 7 and so contradicts 2N - 2. The derivation omits one level.
theory_low.table3-family2-qubits-depth: Section 3.2, Table 3, p.28: inherits the 2N - 2 count that conflicts with Figure 7 (7 qubits for N = 4), lists n qubits in the state where Figure 7 shows 3, and lists gate depth Log2(N) where Equation 12 gives O(Log^2 N). Ceiling brackets are lost in the text layer.
theory_low.family2e-qubit-reuse: Section 3.2, p.28: an authors' design claim about erasure and reuse. The reuse mechanism is in Section 2.5 without proof, and Table 3's 'n total qubits' for 2e is unsupported.
theory_low.family2e-erasure-gate-counts: Section 3.3.3, p.30-31: the 'two CNOT and one Toffoli per discarded qubit' rule is stated from Figure 17. It is not derived, and it uses the 2N - 2 - n qubit count that conflicts with Figure 7.
theory_low.table4-gate-counts: Section 3.2, Table 4, p.27-29: a tabulation. The Hadamard and CSwap columns are derived in 3.3, but the CNOT and CCNot columns and the ancilla counts rest on unproved or conflicting counts. Graded by the weakest.
theory_low.family3-depth-reduction-idea: Section 4, p.31: an authors' design claim (depth k to Log2(k)), shown by example for N = 8 and not proved.
theory_low.family3-parallel-cswap-requirement: Section 4, Figure 26, p.31-32: a description of one layout for N = 8. The claim that all four CSwap gates act on uninvolved qubits is read from the figure, not argued.
theory_low.table5-shor-cat-state: Section 4, Table 5, p.32: a worked three-step state table from Figure 27. The 'Shor cat state' name and the decoupling by slices 5 and 6 are stated, not proved.
theory_low.family3-depth-eq19-eq20: Section 4.1, Equations 19-20, p.32-34: the per-stage depth rests on the figure-based claim that the ancilla circuits have depth ceil(Log2 k). The bound is an informal tally, and the ceiling is lost in the text layer.
theory_low.family3-stirling-sum-log: Section 4.1, Equations 21-24, p.34-35: the log identity is exact, but the step to n Log2 n uses Stirling to first order (an approximation that drops lower terms) and then 'approx Log2 N'. An approximation argued informally, graded by its weaker half.
theory_low.family3-loglog-constant-claim: Section 4.1, Equation 25, p.35: depth O(Log N) follows only by treating Log2 Log2 N as a constant below 10 'in the numerical range of interest'. That is an informal argument, not an asymptotic proof.
theory_low.fig28-loglog-curve: Figure 28, p.36: a value read from a figure is never HIGH on the figure alone. The reading checks out on the rendered page (curve about 6 near N = 1e21).
theory_low.family3-log-qubits-log-depth: The narrowed value matches Sections 4.1 and 5: the O(Log N) depth rests on treating Log2 Log2 N as a constant (Equations 24-25), and the paper tabulates no total qubit count for family #3. An authors' claim and an approximation; the stored one-sentence form drops the caveat.
theory_low.noise-layer-design-mean-2pi-4pi: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 6.1.3, Equation 8, p.29, the RX gate period (so mean 2k pi gives a global phase) is a standard identity, stated and not shown. The reader's reason ('an empirical result') is wrong; it is not empirical.
theory_low.claim-quantum-subroutines-proxy-distance: Section 5.2, p.7-8: 'efficiently generated via the SWAP test' and the exponential speedup rest on cited work [74-77]. A cited result and an authors' claim.
theory_low.vqe-defined-rayleigh-ritz: Section 5.2, p.8: VQE via Rayleigh-Ritz is a field statement cited to [80], and 'LEBM falls as a fitting use-case' is the authors' claim.
theory_low.swap-test-distance-formula: Appendix F, Equations B.2 to B.5, p.25: Pr(0) = 1/2 + 1/2 |<phi|psi>|^2 is shown, but the step to d^2 = 2W |<phi|psi>|^2 follows from the amplitude encoding of B.2 taken from cited work [126, 106] and is not derived in the paper. The Appendix F equation tags (B.x) are also mixed up.
theory_low.swap-test-fidelity-definition: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Appendix F, p.24, the SWAP test measuring the fidelity |<phi|psi>|^2 is a standard fact. The text calls it 'the inner product or overlap', which loosely blurs overlap and its square.
theory_low.matrix-symmetry-reduction-unique-entries: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Appendix F, p.25, the k(k+1)/2 unique entries of a symmetric k by k matrix and the k^2 block count are standard counting, stated and not derived.
theory_low.vqe-pauli-decomposition-hybrid-split: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Appendix G.1, p.26, the standard VQE division of labour (Pauli expectation values on the device, summation and optimization on a classical machine).
theory_low.appendix-hermitian-definition-invertible: Appendix A, Definition A.1, p.17-18: the definition adds 'A is invertible', which is not part of the standard Hermitian definition and is wrong (the zero matrix is Hermitian). A textbook definition stated with an error, so it should not be stored as a fact.
theory_low.appendix-pauli-group-16-elements: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Appendix C, p.22, the Pauli group definition is standard, but '16 elements' holds only for n = 1. P_n has 4^(n+1) elements, 64 for n = 2.
theory_low.appendix-clifford-gate-set: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Appendix C.1, p.22, the generating gate set CNOT, H and P is a standard fact, stated without proof.
theory_low.appendix-fredkin-from-toffoli: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Appendix C.1, p.23, the Fredkin from Toffoli plus two CNOTs identity is standard and cited ([123]), with no derivation.

requote.cranganore-limit-photonic-circuit-model: the stored value joined the cited premise ([94]) to the authors' caveat; the value now holds the caveat alone

value_replace.cranganore-limit-photonic-circuit-model: The authors state that, on photonic machines, circuit synthesis and mapping might not guarantee the best performance.
